pairs.why: Nearly identical scenes, but A's logs and stones are slightly smoother and less grainy, closer to the softly painted real cards than B's more textured wood.
B has a compact flame and smoother painted logs like the real campfire card, while A's logs carry more grain texture and the fire is oversized.
Both are close; A keeps the soft painterly finish with moderate detail, while B leans slightly more uniform and plasticky in its rocks and logs.
A's logs and stones are smoother with soft glow, matching the real cards' gentle finish better than B's slightly grainier wood.
B's logs and stones show more surface grain and roughness, which the lessons mark as too texture-y; A is smoother but not plastic.
B has a cleaner, smoother finish on logs and rocks; A adds more busy texture and detail on the wood and background.
Very close; A's log pile and kettle read slightly cleaner and more like the real cards' soft rendering, B's base stones are a bit lumpier.
B's fire and log stack are built more readably with smooth painted surfaces, while A's logs look a touch more textured and haphazard.
